minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Municipal Building Reuse (Design) Committee reviewed its own notes ahead of a joint meeting with the Board of Selectmen the following Tuesday, covering community outreach gaps, ADA compliance, remaining ARPA funds, and whether to broaden its charge beyond Town Hall and the Ritter building. Members debated whether to bring the roughly $23 million renovation project back to voters at a November special town meeting, discussed engaging the new town manager and new superintendent who were not involved when the plan was developed, and voted to adjourn.

what_happened.line: The committee plans to ask the Select Board Tuesday whether to send the town hall/Ritter renovation back to voters at a November special town meeting.
The committee and Select Board agreed to hold a joint meeting Tuesday evening to decide next steps on the project.
Members discussed looping in the new town manager and new superintendent, who joined after the plan was already developed, including a direct call to the superintendent about space needs.
The committee reviewed unresolved questions on ADA compliance, remaining ARPA funds tied to the project, and whether to widen its charge to other town buildings.

why_it_matters: This sets up a vote residents may be asked to take again at a November special town meeting on the town hall and Ritter building renovation.
ADA compliance and how remaining ARPA funds apply to the project affect what the design can include and what the town still owes on accessibility.
Bringing in the new town manager and superintendent, who were not part of the original planning, could change the project's scope or space needs before any re-vote.
